summary: The retained production thigh overlay is no longer a rotationally symmetric swept tube. It has a torso-aligned anterior axis, bounded quadriceps/hamstring/adductor envelopes, a fuller proximal section, and a narrower distal transition into the solved knee. All five roster identities keep continuous opaque hip-to-knee coverage. Fixed front/profile/rear captures show a less capsule-like seated leg, but the complete character remains visibly synthetic and is not promoted as photoreal.

changed: Production thigh procedural mesh topology and surface profile
Production thigh roll/orientation around the solved hip-to-knee axis
Runtime, native, Python, and renderer capture anatomy contracts
unchanged: Solved crew pose and body proportions
Packaged MetaHuman and CC0 identity geometry
Pelvis, knee, shin, boot, PFD, helmet, hands, and paddle meshes
Animation, collision, crew mass, raft physics, water, rescue, scoring, and progression

implementation.orientation: Local +Z follows the solved hip-to-knee bridge and local +X follows torso forward projected into the thigh-normal plane.
implementation.normals: Finite-difference longitudinal and circumferential surface tangents produce smooth authored normals.
implementation.rejected_bracket: An initial 0.86 depth-scale candidate exposed a hard overlay/body intersection in profile. It was not retained; the final 0.94 envelope keeps the directional shape outside the assembled wetsuit body.

camera_bracket.camera_contract: The baseline and candidate use the same capture_metahuman_production_roster.py full/profile/rear camera transforms, 36 degree FOV, map, lighting, pose, roster, and presentation assets.

improved: The profile silhouette is no longer rotationally symmetric and carries distinct anterior and posterior fullness.
The distal thigh narrows into the assembled knee instead of keeping the old maximum tube radius through the joint.
The broadest and smallest roster profiles preserve the same directional anatomy without losing hip or knee overlap.
The rear silhouette retains proximal mass but tapers toward each knee instead of reading as a constant round lobe.
remaining: The thigh is still a procedural garment overlay over a simplified assembled body, not a fully skinned anatomical deformation.
Hard overlap boundaries and simplified wetsuit reflectance remain visible in profile and rear lighting.
The seated pose, hands, expression, garment/PPE intersections, and surrounding character presentation remain visibly synthetic.
No named character artist or qualified whitewater safety reviewer has approved the anatomy or PPE presentation.

validation.editor_build: SmokeEmIfYouGotEmEditor Mac Development succeeded after the final 0.94 depth-envelope refinement.
validation.renderer_capture: capture_metahuman_production_roster.py completed all five identities and failed closed on vertex count, anterior alignment, continuity, and centreline coverage.
validation.benign_engine_warning: The renderer process emitted the existing google.com/generate_204 connectivity timeout during shutdown; it did not affect local capture output.

required_external_acceptance_gates: A named character artist must approve the front/profile/rear anatomy and garment deformation across the full body-profile roster.
A qualified whitewater safety reviewer must approve the complete seated posture, PPE fit, mobility, and paddle-ready presentation.
The product owner must approve the integrated in-river moving-camera presentation before photoreal or M9 promotion.
